summary: A quiet strip across the top of every page of a site, above its header: one lasting, site-wide fact the reader should know wherever they land, with at most one link to learn more.

children: Paid plans open in 2027. Teams that request access by 31 March 2027 stay free, with no end date.

whenToUse: A fact that holds across the whole site for weeks or months and matters wherever a reader lands: a pricing commitment, a change of terms, a planned shutdown date.
Above the site header, full bleed, on marketing and documentation pages. One per site.
Give at most one way on: either the whole strip as a link (href) to the page that explains it, or one DS Link after the message (action). Prefer href when the message itself says enough.
harbor (default) on pages that open on the plain page color; neutral when the page under the strip opens with a Harbor zone of its own.
whenNotToUse: A mode the page is in (previewing a past change, editing): use Banner.
A message about the page's content or a failure: use Alert.
Confirming an action the user just took: use a Toast.
Inside an app (Studio, Library): app pages carry state, not announcements.
Promotions, countdowns or urgency: a strip states a fact, it never pushes.

dos.title: State the fact and the date
dos.text: One or two short sentences a reader can repeat: what is true, and until when.

children: Paid plans open in 2027. Teams that request access by 31 March 2027 stay free, with no end date.

dos.title: Neutral under a Harbor page header
dos.text: One Harbor zone per screen: when the page opens with a Harbor header, the strip takes the subtle ground.

children: Our terms of service change on 1 March 2027.

donts.title: Urgency or a sales pitch
donts.text: "Only 3 days left, upgrade now!" turns a fact into a promotion. Readers learn to ignore strips that push.

donts.title: A Button in the strip
donts.text: The strip links to where the fact is explained. An action that changes something belongs on that page.

children: Teams that request access by 31 March 2027 stay free.

accessibility: A complementary landmark (aside) named by its label, so screen reader users can find it in the landmarks list or skip it.
Not a live region and not dismissible: it is part of the page when it loads, and it never moves focus.
The icon is decorative (aria-hidden); the words carry the message.
The link is a real DS Link, reached with Tab before the site header.
harbor uses color.bg.zone with color.text.default (13.07:1 light, 14.05:1 dark) and color.text.link (7.03:1, 6.47:1); neutral uses color.bg.subtle with color.text.default.
contentGuidelines: One or two short sentences, a fact and its date. Sentence case, no exclamation marks.
At most one emphasis (strong) on the word that matters.
With action, the link text names where it goes ("Read the commitment"), not "Learn more". With href, the message is the link text: no extra words.

anatomy.strip: Container: a complementary landmark, full bleed, one centred row that wraps
anatomy.harbor: Harbor appearance: the light Harbor zone (default)
anatomy.message: The line: icon, text and link, centred together
anatomy.action: One DS Link to learn more; on phones it takes its own line
